alignments.note: One substantive rendered by a two-word phrase; men alone is any men, so the head is young under rule 31.
The waw takes the closing connective of the correlative pair, rule 14.

The particle is itself what the opening correlative Both says, so it takes that word and the waw takes only the and, exactly as rule 14 gives the both of a min-ad range to the preposition; the competing reading would give both ... and to the waw alone and leave the particle unrepresented.
Substantival adjective with the generic noun the ASV supplies to make it a noun phrase, rule 46; head on the word carrying the lexeme under rule 31.
The comitative preposition is the morpheme the ASV's connective answers to, so it takes the written and under rule 11 rather than leaving the word added.

review_notes: Both ... and is one correlative pair over two morphemes; the particle takes the opening word because it is itself what that word says, and the waw takes the closing and.
Old men is read as a substantival adjective with a supplied generic under rule 46, headed on Old by rule 31's subtraction.
